name: CT-996
lead: CT-996 is an investigational oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist from Roche, also registered under the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron [2][3]. It is being developed as a once-daily pill for weight loss and for type 2 diabetes, so its appearance relevance is fat loss: people interested in a leaner body and face follow GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide, and an oral option is a topic of interest in that community.

Small-molecule oral GLP-1 agonists are a class designed to avoid the injection requirement of peptide drugs; a 2025 review describes them as acting at non-canonical sites in the receptor with biased G-protein signalling [1]. CT-996 came to Roche through its acquisition of Carmot Therapeutics, announced on 4 December 2023 for USD 2.7 billion in cash plus up to USD 400 million in milestones, which then described CT-996 as a once-daily oral agent in phase 1 [8].

Roche reported topline phase 1 results in July 2024, describing a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of 6.1% within four weeks in participants with obesity but without type 2 diabetes [11]. Phase 2 studies in obesity and type 2 diabetes have since been registered [3][4]. It is not approved anywhere and is not available outside trials.

paras: A review of small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonists says these nonpeptidic agents act mainly through non-canonical orthosteric sites within the receptor transmembrane domain, producing G-protein-biased signalling with reduced beta-arrestin-mediated adverse effects, and notes that orforglipron has advanced furthest in the class [1]. Peptide GLP-1 drugs are injected; a pill avoids that route [1].

Roche's phase 1 announcement, as reported by trade press, described CT-996 as a biased agonist that activates cAMP signalling with minimal beta-arrestin recruitment, and said blood levels were little affected whether participants were fasting or had eaten a high-fat meal, suggesting it could be taken regardless of meal timing [11].

Roche announced a definitive agreement to acquire Carmot Therapeutics on 4 December 2023 for USD 2.7 billion in cash at closing plus up to USD 400 million in milestone payments. The assets included CT-996, an oral once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist in phase 1 for obesity with or without type 2 diabetes, CT-388, a once-weekly subcutaneous dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, and CT-868, a daily dual agonist for type 1 diabetes with overweight [8]. Registrations since then use the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron [3].

The phase 1 study (CT-996-201) was double-blind and placebo-controlled. Part 1 enrolled 40 overweight or obese participants on single ascending doses; part 2 enrolled three sequential cohorts of 25 participants with obesity but without type 2 diabetes on multiple ascending doses [11]. Roche reported a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of 6.1% within four weeks, mostly mild or moderate gastrointestinal adverse events, and no discontinuations due to adverse events [11]. Roche's chief medical officer Levi Garraway said the company was pleased to see clinically meaningful weight loss [11]. A third part in 30-person cohorts with type 2 diabetes was planned [11]. Analyst commentary reported in news coverage noted the early time point and small sample size, so the figure comes from a short, small study.

A completed phase 1 study in overweight or obese participants and people with type 2 diabetes enrolled 94 people from May 2023 [2]. A phase 2 study of daily oral tifeglipron in 352 people with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related comorbidity began in July 2025 and is listed as completed [3]. A 330-person phase 2 study from August 2025 compares different doses with placebo or semaglutide in type 2 diabetes [4].

Further phase 1 studies registered include a drug-interaction study of approved medications in 36 healthy participants (2025) [6], a multiple-dose study in 30 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (2026) [7], a statin interaction study in 40 people (2025) [9], and a renal impairment study of 60 participants (2026) [10]. No results have been published.

CT-996 is one of several oral GLP-1 candidates under development alongside orforglipron [1]. Roche has said it hopes CT-996 could support glycemic control and weight loss and possibly serve as maintenance therapy after weight loss with injectable drugs [11]. It is not available outside clinical trials.

card.summary: Roche's experimental oral GLP-1 pill, with registered phase 2 trials and no results seen yet.
card.note: Investigational; no published efficacy data found.

quick.overview:
CT-996 (tifeglipron) is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist from Roche for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Phase 2 trials are registered; results were not found.
quick.mechanism: A small-molecule agonist of the GLP-1 receptor taken by mouth, rather than a peptide injection.
quick.risks: No published safety or efficacy data were found. Not approved.

chain: Activates the GLP-1 receptor from a once-daily pill
Reduced appetite and body weight in trial participants
Lower body fat, leaner body and face
angle.text: CT-996 is being developed as an oral weight-loss medicine, so its relevance to appearance runs through fat loss. People who follow GLP-1 drugs for a leaner look watch oral candidates because they avoid injections.
